chapter: Connie's Inn, Duke Ellington and the Swingland band
title: Piano style: chords in ensemble, single line or octaves in solos
summary: Horace played chords with the ensemble and single-note or octave lines in solos; Hines-style octaves worked on slow tunes like Sweet Lorraine but not fast ones.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: With -- getting back to the piano style, and you say the closeness to Earl Hines' style, were you doing quite a lot of chording or was it still a certain amount of stride bass, or --
I would play chords when the ensemble thing was going, but as soon as you got to the solo, it would be the -- sometimes the one finger, and of course, Earl would play like in octaves, you know.
It would move. It would swing. It was a rather awkward thing to do, especially if you wanted to make some fast passages, and you would have to go back to the one-finger stuff.
But mostly, if you had a tune like
"Sweet Lorraine", you know, and you'd be --
Well, then you could use your octave.
